#4065. itch.io will soon let you filter games with genAI disclosures out of your search results on the site, after admitting it was previously "critically lacking"

itch.io has unfortunately, much like Steam, long had an issue with genAI content being uploaded in droves, drowning out perfectly good games made by human hands. The apparent standard method against this, voluntary genAI disclosure, has been itch's primary tool to combat this wave of low-quality slop, but hasn't worked out too well; itch revealed a few days ago that 'the number of game pages being created per-day has doubled in the past two months'. Now, in attempts to further combat this, beyond just game assets requiring a genAI disclosure to upload as they have for two years, itch will be expanding the mandatory disclosure to tabletop games, books, comics, and soundtracks, as well as adding a 'no AI' filter directly into the search function.

itch noted in this announcement that its previous moderation of genAI use in projects had been "critically lacking", presumably referring to the unfathomable exponential increase in games being uploaded in the past few months by people who don't give a fuck about creating anything themselves and happily contribute to the death of the planet. itch went on to post "Just deleted a couple terabytes of ai slop" which, I mean, sure, cool! And, look, as many, many people in itch's replies have pointed out, this is not the same as outright banning AI.

Unfortunately, my question at that point becomes: how? itch is not Steam, not a storefront backed by a gigantic corporation with support staff and quality assurance (which, you know, hasn't helped Steam much either). itch is one full-time employee with several contractors and volunteers. If there is a site-wide ban on genAI, people who use genAI will just start lying and sneaking it into their projects anyway. So, then, users just report the offenders, surely? This then requires a manual verification system, which, as is suggested by the sheer amount of games being uploaded every day, is just not feasible, let alone for a team as small as itch. And, frankly, I don't have a better solution here! This is fucked! What itch is doing is, currently, kinda the best it can right now?

itch is a beautiful thing that allows for people who just want to start making games, making art, making music, making books, to have a free space to share it with the world, and gain eyes on their work as well as necessary feedback to improve. It's less of a store and more of a forum for creators and self-published games to interact, guide one another to new, niche, cool shit. Hell, I made a visual novel and posted it on there, becoming another one of those millions of people for whom itch is a valuable platform for first creations. To have this vital space on a path to ruin as a result of the same vile tech that is also on the verge of pushing the global economy over a cliff due to its creators being caught in their multi-year lies is not a future I hope for itch. This is a step in the right direction, and one I genuinely hope pans out well for it in the long run.

#4064. The Rings of Power season 3's new heroic Orc character offers a fresh perspective on Middle-earth

Join the GamesRadar community for quick access. Enter your email below and we'll send confirmation, and sign you up to our newsletter.

Keep exploring and earning more as a member.

Bringing all the latest movie news, features, and reviews to your inbox

Unlock instant access to exclusive member features.

Get full access to premium articles, exclusive features and a growing list of member rewards.

'Orc with an arc' Marnûkh is something we've never seen before in The Lord of the Rings

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Adapting Tolkien's sprawling canon of Middle-Earth lore, The Rings of Power explores ideas and locations that we don't get to see in the main Lord of the Rings trilogy. We visit Númenor and the Southlands, and witness a new side to characters like Galadriel and Gandalf. But as the show began to spend more time on the rise of Sauron, one perspective seemed a little underdeveloped: that of the Orcs, the much-maligned race who make up most of Sauron's army.

In The Rings of Power season 3, we finally experience more of that Orcish perspective, represented by a new character named Marnûkh (Adam Young), "an Orc with an arc." Arriving in episode 2, his storyline echoes the period in The Lord of the Rings when Gollum guides Frodo and Sam through Mordor.

Marnûkh's role revolves around leading Galadriel and Arondir to the Orcish prison of Gundabad, so they can rescue an elven smith who has been imprisoned there for years. If they can save her, then they can undermine Sauron's plan to make the One Ring – but it takes a while for the elves to accept Marnûkh's motivations.

In Tolkien's world, we're not encouraged to see Orcs as individual people with relatable feelings. They tend to be depicted as intrinsically malevolent and repulsive, functioning as anonymous cannon fodder in Sauron's wars. In turn, Tolkien's influence over other fantasy properties like Dungeons and Dragons has led to a lot of debate around the concept of fantasy racism, and whether it's offensive to depict an entire race of people as evil, ugly, and subservient to their villainous master. The Rings of Power has to contend with that question, and while the show doesn't stray too far from Tolkien's vision, the first two seasons already introduced the idea of Orcs forming their own faction to rebel against Sauron's rule.

Season 1 positioned the fallen Elf Adar as one of the show's most prominent original characters, leading an army of Orcs who want to establish their own independent territory. Adar's leadership is brutal, and his followers are far from morally upstanding, but their existence introduces the possibility that one day, the Orcs might live in peace.

In Tolkien's world, we're not encouraged to see Orcs as individual people with relatable feelings.

Of course, that dream ends with Adar's demise in season 2. Then during the five-year time jump between seasons, it seems that his former followers have fallen in line with Sauron's goals. Any dissidents have either been killed or are operating in secret, like Marnûkh, who seeks out Galadriel and tells her about Sauron's plans for a "master ring," seeing her as a potential ally because she was previously willing to negotiate with Adar. "If he forges that ring, we'll be nothing but food for his enemy's swords," says Marnûkh, neatly explaining his lack of loyalty toward Sauron.

If Galadriel can free this elven smith from Gundabad before Sauron arrives, then Sauron won't gain the knowledge he requires to forge the One Ring. Believing that Marnûkh cannot be trusted with Galadriel's safety, Arondir joins them on their quest, creating an uncomfortable dynamic where Arondir constantly expects Marnûkh to betray them, while Marnûkh purposefully gets on his nerves by being crass and abrasive.

Objectively speaking, Marnûkh is making a heroic choice that could easily lead to his own death. However, Arondir struggles to accept that Marnûkh can be trusted, because Arondir has spent his entire life viewing Orcs as the enemy.

Arondir probably wouldn't maintain this level of bias against one of Sauron's human followers who decided to switch sides, but Marnûkh is extremely Orcish in a way that irritates Galadriel and Arondir's elven sensibilities, making puerile jokes and catching live butterflies to keep as a snack. So when it comes to Tolkien's rather one-dimensional view of Orcs, Marnûkh allows The Rings of Power to have its cake and eat it too. He's stereotypically Orcish in pretty much every respect, yet he still becomes a trustworthy ally in the war against Sauron.

The Dark Wizard's identity in The Rings of Power has been revealed, and it's a key Lord of the Rings character

Once they reach Gundabad, Galadriel and Arondir truly have to put their life in Marnûkh's hands. Pretending that they're his prisoners, he leads them into a fortress full of Orcs who would happily torture them to death. Then he guides Arondir to the cells, and even helps him free Galadriel's long-lost husband Celeborn when they find him inside.

In episode 4's closing scenes, as the elves and Marnûkh prepare to flee the fortress, Arondir actually saves Marnûkh's life in battle and helps him to his feet, signifying that he has finally managed to look past his hatred of orcs. Arondir ends up dying later in this scene, while Marnûkh's fate remains ambiguous, having been struck down without explicitly dying onscreen.

As the show's most significant Orcish character to date, Marnûkh invites us to question how much of the Orcs' treacherous, villainous reputation is down to nature, and how much is the result of nurture, shaped by their experiences under the thumb of a tyrant. Marnûkh clearly sees himself as a victim of Sauron's rule – although with most other orcs still fighting on Sauron's side, it's easy for the show to keep portraying them as enemies who the heroes can slaughter without guilt. It's a tricky balance to strike within this season's wartime narrative, but Marnûkh's role adds some much-needed depth to the Orcs' place in Middle-Earth.

The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power season 3 episodes 1-4 are streaming now on Prime Video. Don't miss an episode with our Rings of Power season 3 release schedule and read our verdict on the new season in our Rings of Power season 3 review.

She also co-hosts the movie review podcast Overinvested.

#4063. "There’s always a night when Rome burns": South Of Midnight director says that Xbox funding it was "unsustainable", at least in hindsight

"I didn’t know exactly when it would be, but I was always worried about it"

Compulsion Games parted ways with former owners Xbox, having landed on the long list of things Microsoft were determined to ditch as part of multi-round mass cuts this year. Now, South of Midnight creative director David Sears has suggested that an eventual pulling of the rug was something he feared throughout the game's development, to the point where he seemingly doesn't think he'd have funded it if he'd been in the shoes of Xbox execs.

In an interview with MinnMax, Sears - who left Compulsion in March 2025 - outlined that ideally games big publishers put out aim to fall into one of two buckets. They either make lots of money or increase the prestige of the brand by becoming cultural touchstones across multiple generations. Obviously doing both is the perfect outcome, but Sears pegged South of Midnight as being more geared towards the latter camp. The likes of Double Fine's Keeper and Obsidian's Pentiment are other games which off the top of my head could be said to fit that same mold. The issue, of course, is that when push comes to shove, it's the games which can show a strong bottom line at any given moment which make the best case for their studios' short term survival if cash is tight.

So, South of Midnight lived in a risky place, with Sears recalling: "I literally told people. I was like, yeah, this could be terrible because somebody is going to say, one day, 'The money tap, we're closing those floodgates' and that's going to have really traumatic results downstream". The interviewer then asked Sears if what he was getting at is that, while he's glad Xbox funded South of Midnight, he might not have done so or at least cut the funding earlier if he was in charge of the console maker.

"Yeah, probably," Sears replied. "I mean, I wanted to make it. No doubt. Obviously, because we made it. Would I have turned off someone else's money flow before South of Midnight? Yeah, because I'm not completely selfless. It just seems like, in hindsight at least, it was unsustainable. So, of course, it was going to have a 'shocking' outcome. I mean, it's easy to dissect it now, right? But at the time, I would talk to other directors and [they] would be like, 'How is this happening? I mean, how did we get so lucky? Is this a golden era?' And I would always be like, 'For now'. There's always a night when Rome burns and I didn't know exactly when it would be, but I was always worried about it."

Notably, Sears added that in his view modern Microsoft showed a "more humane" side than the version of the company that existed in the 90s and early 2000s by giving studios like Compulsion a chance to spin out on their own rather than simply shuttering them outright once they were deemed surplus to requirements.

Given the director's no longer at Compulsion, it seems he'll not have a say on what their next game looks like, but as a newly indie studio one would imagine they'll have a keen eye on the bottom line.

#4062. Marathon To Add New Co-Op Roguelite Mode, Social Spaces, And Other Major Features In December

It's beginning to look a lot like Destiny

Bungie isn't prepared to let its extraction shooter go quietly. Instead, Marathon's upcoming 'Symbiosis' update arrives on December 8, bringing a whole host of new PvE and PvP modes. Having just finished watching the new gameplay trailer above, I've got to say, It's giving off plenty of Destiny vibes.

I'm a big, big fan of Marathon, but that's not to say I don't think the game needs a shake-up. It clearly needs something to keep things ticking along. I can't help but feel extremely hyped now that Bungie has shared a first look at all the new content coming next month.

The most interesting addition of the bunch is 'Limbo': a new social space. This is where runners can hang out, chat, test weapons at the firing range and challenge each other in the duelling pit. It reminds me of The Tower from Destiny 2.

Social spaces play a huge role in fostering a sense of community in games, and Bungie knows all about that. Just look at the time Destiny players gathered at The Tower en masse to mourn the passing of Lance Reddick, the voice of Commander Zavala.

Beyond that, 'Expedition' is a new co-op PvE roguelite mode. No PvP, just you and your crew going against new threats. PlayStation.Blog shared an official description of the the new mode:

"Expedition: Phase 1 of a new PvE-only mode built around a three-run series. Play solo or with a crew, face new combat and environmental challenges without PvP threats, and use Flash Boosts to shape your build during a run."

If battling it out against other runners is more your style, Marathon is getting it's first PvP mode, Deathmatch (Beta) pitting quick 3v3 matches against one another. Personally, I think this is a great way to let players get used to the game's arsenal of weapons and gadgets without the time commitment that comes with extraction.

There are a few other new bits and bobs coming to Marathon in December, including a new runner shell, which we'll cover below:

To coincide with the Symbiosis update, Bungie will also be hosting an Open Play Week starting December 8, allowing new players to download and play Marathon for free.

What do you think PXers? Are you fussed about Marathon? Let us know what you think in the comments below.

Craig is a Staff Writer and former Video Producer at Pure Xbox, where he covers the biggest games in the world of Xbox.

#4061. GTA 6 on PS5 Is PS Store's Most Pre-Ordered Digital Game in History

It was always going to be big, but with a week until release, Rockstar has now confirmed that GTA 6 is the most pre-ordered digital game in PS Store history.

Confirmation comes courtesy of the PS Blog, in a post from Sony’s Tim Turi.

“GTA 6 is now the most pre-ordered game in the history of PS Store. Given this unprecedented demand, we’ve joined with Rockstar Games to allow players to start pre-loading the game nine days early, so they’re ready to play on launch day. We’ve also adopted a rolling midnight launch by country, beginning at 12:00AM NZDT in New Zealand and running across the globe as respective countries hit midnight on 19th November.”

You can learn more about when you’ll be able to play in our dedicated GTA 6 release times guide, so keep that bookmarked for 19th November.

Digital pre-orders for GTA 6 have been available since 25th June, so Rockstar has had a long time to build up numbers.

It’s worth reiterating that physical versions are following a “code-in-box” format, so there’s less incentive to purchase at retail, too.

(Although in a recent Push Square poll, a remarkable 23% of our readers did say they’d be plumping up for the boxed version.)

Record-breaking pre-orders like this are significant as the PS Store has been selling digital games for over a decade now; that it’s set a new record with over a week to spare and hype still building is remarkable.

While we don’t have actual numbers, Rockstar’s said they’re “exceeding” its external expectations.

Analyst firm Sensor Tower predicts 9.69 million pre-orders have been placed, with an astonishing 75% of those sales commanded by the PS5 version.

It’s worth noting that this milestone comes at a time of deep unrest among PS5 players, who’ve continuously spammed the platform holder with proclamations of ‘No Disc, No Buy’ in the aftermath of its decision to stop shipping physical games in 2028.

Sony recently reported year-over-year increases to its monthly active users, during a period in which enthusiasts mobilised a “blackout” of its platform.

Irrespective of fan frustration, it looks like Rockstar’s latest open world is days away from registering the biggest digital launch in industry history.

#4060. Arc Raiders devs Embark insist that using genAI for voice lines was necessary, as "actors would just go crazy if they had to read all of that"

Despite taking the voice performances of actors and feeding them into machines to spurt out AI-generated mimicry, Embark CCO Stefan Strandberg insists that "we are not in the industry of replacing actors." In a new video posted to the Arc Raiders channel focused on audio design, Strandberg refers back to the infamous use of genAI in Arc Raiders to generate voice lines based on real voice actors' performances, something which the game was heavily (and rightly) criticised for before and since its release.

In that linked piece (thanks Oisin!), CEO Patrick Söderlund stated that they have been replacing lines that were originally generated with actual recorded lines, presumably because Arc Raiders has made quite a bit of money and now they feel that they can continue paying actors to record more lines, rather than just scraping their talents and avoiding the dreaded fee of paying professionals for their work. This choice already came after their previous game, The Finals, was heavily criticised for the exact same thing, which is just a fascinating series of decisions to consider.

In the video, audio director Bence Pajor explains that the apparent reason for the use of AI was to avoid the "stress" of having to work around actors' availability, as they may be busy working on other projects when Embark decides that a new feature needs new voice lines recorded. Pings, quests, and in-level mission briefings were thus generated using training data based on existing actors' recordings, saving the need to actually get anyone back in a studio or pay them for their time. Citing the amount of variables that the ping system creates, Pajor claims it "becomes too impractical to record every possible version of something. The actors would just go crazy if they had to read all of that", which is a take that falls apart if you consider the simple fact that games of this scope (or bigger) have been managing to work around actors' availability for as long as genAI has not been an accessible technology, which has been almost all of the time that video games have existed. Isn't it crazy that games like Disco Elysium and Baldur's Gate 3 had so, so much recorded dialogue, all without genAI? Or fellow live service shooter Apex Legends, which has been adding and adjusting voice lines via updates for years? How could they possibly have managed it?

Voice actresses Jo Rideout and Diana Gardner, who play Shani and Celeste respectively, are also featured speaking on their characters' relationships as well as their experience working within this hybrid model of recording and generating voices. Gardner notes that "if they only need an hour of my time for a couple call-outs that are short, then I don't have to cancel other shoots or some other project that might also be interesting. So in that way, I feel quite good about it." She then explains that "the contract seemed fair…so it was a no-brainer in that sense. But I didn't know what to expect once I heard the voice come out. I was like, 'Can I take ownership for the performance?' This is hours of work that I've put in, but can I take ownership for the final product? No."

Strandberg goes on to elaborate on his comment on not replacing actors by saying that "We are not in the industry of replacing actors, actually, I think quite the opposite. We should celebrate the performance, and we should give them more space." While Embark's audio team are indeed working on replacing the generated lines with actual performances, that doesn't change the fact that the choice to use AI in the first place was one made simply to save money in not paying actors for their specific work and get the game out the door faster — effectively the 'we'll fix it in post' of games development. While I can respect Garner's awareness that it means she can prioritise other projects when necessary, there is that notable tinge of regret in not being able to take ownership for her hours of work. Fundamentally, Embark has demonstrated its willingness to cut talent to cut costs, seemingly happy to post PR videos implying they had no choice due to the game's scope, and that isn't something a company just goes back on once they realise how 'efficient' it can be.

#4059. Round Up: The Reviews Are In For Pikmin 4 - Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy

Following the anticipated return of Zelda: Ocarina of Time last week, Nintendo has now released Pikmin 4 - Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy. The critic reviews have now gone live. If you haven't already seen ours, we gave it seven stars, calling it a pleasant but perplexing piecemeal.

"Overall, £8/$10 is a small price to pay for some minor new features and a fun little mode that'll keep me entertained over the coming year, but it's more of a budding shoot right now than the full-bloom upgrade."

Mini Review Pikmin 4 - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy (Switch 2) - Pleasant But Perplexingly Piecemeal

And here's what other critics had to say:

"For late-bloomers who have yet to experience the magic that is Pikmin 4, the Nintendo Switch 2 Edition is the best place to start. Not only is native 4K resolution a significant improvement that allows the colourful world of Pikmin to shine brighter than ever before, Dandori Academy brings some worthwhile new content, held back only by Nintendo’s puzzling monthly stage distribution method. While not quite as extravagant as some of the other Nintendo Switch 2 Editions we’ve seen in recent memory, the lower-end $10 for the Upgrade Pack is an appropriate price point for what Pikmin 4 has to offer on Nintendo Switch 2; with the base game being in a class of its own."

"The main takeaway is that Pikmin 4 is still excellent, and I was grateful to transfer my save file from the Switch version (and I was tempted to start a new game + save), but Dandori Academy is not a strong incentive to return if you already played the game. It is a nice bonus and an interesting concept that reimagines the familiar time trial mode featured in plenty of video games, but the original campaign is still the main attraction."

"Pikmin 4 still remains one of my favourite titles released on the original Nintendo Switch, but unfortunately this update has left me feeling more than a little underwhelmed. While the game has seen a visual upgrade and the Oatchi commands are certainly a novel addition, the drip-feeding of its major new Dandori Academy content proves more frustrating than anything. More Pikmin is never a bad thing, but having to wait months to see it all, well… that’s a drag."

"Pikmin 4 is already a great time; Pikmin 4 – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy is just the 4K cherry on top. If you don’t own the original Switch version, then this is an easy recommendation; if you’re here for the upgrade/additions, then the visual upgrade will help. Dandori Academy won’t be for everyone, but over the next year it will continue to add extra challenges. The cheaper upgrade price point helps make it an easier recommendation."

Final Fantasy 7 Revelation director Naoki Hamaguchi talks hitting the slopes in the trilogy's final chapter

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The original Final Fantasy 7 might have featured heaps of command battles and a dense, complex mythos, but it's more than its ecologically-forward story that connected us to the game's world. Filled with a whole planet of towns to explore and people to chat with, Cloud and his RPG party frequently take time to embed themselves in these communities. Taking part in activities and minigames is a huge part of that. Who among us didn't spend whole afternoons just chilling at the Gold Saucer like we were taking a real theme park break?

One of the Final Fantasy 7 Remake trilogy's greatest strengths is understanding this appeal and building upon it as the perspective moves from an abstracted top-down view into a more realistic scale – and Final Fantasy 7 Revelation is aiming to take that even further with its scope of activities. While some people might be eager to see what the final game in the series will reveal about Aerith's fate, or just what is going on with the formerly deceased Zack Fair, we have more urgent questions for director Naoki Hamaguchi. What about snowboarding? What about my precious cards?!

"The snowboarding minigame is just essential to FF7 as a whole," says Hamaguchi. He's totally correct. Cloud dealing with emotional trauma and delving deep into haunting research notes before tearing down a mountain while grabbing sick air is a vital part of the PS1 classic's identity. "I feel like that's what fans are expecting," he says, and the team are keen to deliver on that promise.

With the remake trilogy drawing to a close early 2027, we get ready for the epic conclusion with our Final Fantasy 7 Revelation Big Preview across hands-on impressions, dev access, and deep dives into the whole adventure so far.

"It's not just going to be a minigame you access through the Gold Saucer," confirms Hamaguchi. "It's actually going to be involved in the main story as well." While this detailed remake and pseudo-sequel trilogy dig deeper into some of the story's themes and seriousness, it's historically not been afraid to show its sillier side. If how the team expanded on Wall Market in Final Fantasy 7 Remake is anything to go by, there's every chance snowboarding here will be played straight while adding plenty of flourish.

"In terms of when exactly you're going to play it during the game in the main story, I'll say I hope you stay tuned!" adds Hamaguchi. Though these remakes alter the events of the original game at points, most of the main beats are intact, so it'll be interesting to see if this tease means it'll shift context slightly. Going off the PS1 original, I'd expect to see it fairly early in Final Fantasy 7 Revelation. Yet, I could imagine it becoming a fist-pumping sequence closer to a climax instead. Who's to say there even will be a traditional fight against Sephiroth instead of Cloud and the silver-haired villain settling their differences by shredding the slopes?

Final Fantasy 7 Revelation is boasting even more content than its already stuffed predecessor and middle-entry in the trilogy, Final Fantasy 7 Rebirth. Able to hop in the Highwind airship to explore a planetary-sized open world, that'll likely mean plenty of returning activities and minigames for Cloud and the cast to check up on – especially back at the Gold Saucer.

Rather than resurrecting minigames from the original FF7, though, a card game that stole our hearts in FF7 Rebirth will be returning in FF7 Revelation. Taking cues from the series' history with card-based side-activities – most notably Triple Triad across Final Fantasy 8 and Final Fantasy 14 – Queen's Blood is a lane-based monster-slinging card game that saw us taking on all manner of opponents throughout the last adventure, including a cruise ship tournament and a mysterious conspiracy. The best Final Fantasy games usually have some sort of side-diversion I become obsessed with.

Sign up to our Switch 2 Spotlight newsletter to make sure you get the very latest news on Nintendo's new console and its games every week

"Ever since the launch of FF7 Rebirth, we've [had] a lot of warm, positive reception specifically to the Queen's Blood minigame. We saw a lot of people saying, 'Oh, are you guys making a standalone game for Queen's Blood?' or 'Oh, it's going to be in Part Three, right?'," laughs Hamaguchi. Other RPGs with card games have indeed made that standalone leap – and with the recent The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered I've been hooked on Gwent once again. Soon enough, Queen's Blood will have me equally hypnotized.

Final Fantasy 7 Revelation boss doesn't want to hear your Rebirth minigame discourse: "I don't think that discussion really gets to the heart of the matter"

"We saw a lot of those [comments]. So, from early on, there really was no other option for us – like, yeah, we've definitely got to put it into Part Three, so that was a given from the start!" says Hamaguchi. This time around, the wolf-like party member Red XIII will take the lead in the new Queen's Blood storyline, building on his role as the enigmatic challenger on the cruise in FF7 Rebirth.

The new storyline will seemingly be its own self-contained activity with rewards that just feed back into the deckbuilding so those who don't like it can safely move on. It's a shift in the reward system that stops players who are only interested in certain types of play feeling strong-armed into completing everything if they don't want to, which wasn't the case with FF7 Rebirth. For FF7 Revelation, "what's important is communicating to the player, making it very easy to see what you're going to get for going through that content, what kind of rewards you can expect," says Hamaguchi.

Besides the new narrative content taking Red XIII through his Queen's Blood matches, the card game will also be receiving updates. "The gameplay of Queen's Blood, it was really good – we felt that it was in a pretty good state, and a lot of fans were pretty happy about it too – but we didn't want to just rehash the same exact thing. We did polish the system again. We are implementing new rules and mechanics into [it]." says Hamaguchi.

Aspects like balance have been a big point of discussion on the team, with a lot of tweaks throughout development to get it right. "We are pretty confident that we're able to show, like, a new side of Queen's Blood that fans did not see in Rebirth." Say no more. Just deal me in!

#4056. Workers & Resources: Soviet Republic's next DLC is set to expand the city building sim into the one place not corrupted by capitalism: SPACE

Following not the inherent liberal capitalistic framework of city builders like SimCity but instead a revolutionary (sorry) interpretation of planning and logistical simulation that prioritises centralisation and minute detail, Hooded Horse and 3DIVISION's Workers & Resources: Soviet Republic offers a tense, socialist look at what a citybuilder could be. Fellow contributor Sin Vega, in her 1.0 review, described it like this: "You have to build things to demolish things. That might be Workers & Resources in a nutshell. You're not managing budgets (money is exclusively for imports/exports), you're organising stuff." Now, having previously expanding out of the Soviet Republic and across the globe with the World Maps DLC, the next step for socialist citybuilding is, of course, space. Our Edwin outright predicted this two years ago, correctly calling that "the logical endgame here is to go to space." Good on him.

The Space Program DLC, set to release on November 23rd, will add a variety of new technologies and types of industry to the builder. It looks like it'll focus on not only the actual rockets that get into space, and the spectacle of it all, but also the huge amounts of science and industry that get to the point of rockets not exploding upon takeoff. For example, while it's all well and good for Space Program's scientists to be able to design rockets that are capable of remaining together for long enough to land safely, the designs they dream of still have to be built, meaning that industrial pipelines must be effectively centralised to ensure that every single component is of high quality and arriving in the required quantity.

The update also specifies the Sputnik and Vostok programs as elements of the expansion, implying a close historical aspect to it — though, elsewhere, "an unprecedented duel with nature" is mentioned, which is referring to either the simple harshness of space or aliens. Jury's out. A 1960s campaign will be a star feature of the DLC, which is described as a place for players to learn the new mechanics "in relative peace, surrounded by a happy, healthy, and economically stable utopia." What an idea.

#4055. PS Plus Pulls Plug on PC Streaming After Fewer Than 1% Used It

Members of the manufacturer’s most expensive tier can currently stream and play titles from the PS Plus Premium catalogue using a PC app, which will be discontinued next month.

Curiously, this service has always been limited to PS4 and PS3 titles – it never expanded support to the PS5 library.

The pages on PlayStation.com where you used to be able to download the software have already been removed in anticipation.

Writing on the PS Blog, Sony’s Adam Michel said:

“PlayStation believes in providing high-quality experiences to our players, and we regularly review offerings to ensure we are focusing on experiences our members value most. With a very small number of eligible PS Plus Premium members (less than 0.4%) using the PS Plus app on PC, making this change allows us to focus on enhancing high-quality experiences that more of our members want to use. As a result, the PS Plus cloud streaming app on PC will no longer be available.”

Once upon a time, I did temporarily use PS Now streaming on my laptop when I went through a period where I didn’t have access to my consoles. But I haven’t used the feature since.

I don’t think Sony promoted this particularly prominently, so I expect many fans may only be finding out about it now.

But I think this is probably part of a broader push by the Japanese giant to move its software off PC. Internally, it’s pivoted away from porting its first-party single player games to the platform. Now it’s ceasing streaming as well.

It should be stressed that PS Plus Premium cloud streaming will remain available on the PS5, PS4, and PS Portal. There will also be no changes to Remote Play functionality.

Will you be affected by this at all? Given the numbers touted in Sony’s article, I can’t imagine many of you will have used this.

#4054. I'm sad that the Like A Dragon creator's new studio is closing, but I wish their now-cancelled debut Gang of Dragon wasn't just LAD again

Less than a year after the announcement of their first game, and only four years after the studio's creation, Gang of Dragon developers Nagoshi Studio have been dissolved by a shareholders' resolution (thanks, Gematsu.) That also means a premature end for Gang of Dragon, which was announced at last year's Game Awards with a flashy trailer featuring Like a Dragon-esque realistic visuals, combat and exploration through Kabukicho, a couple new elements like actual gunplay and car chases, as well as the star power of actor Ma Dong-seok (a.k.a. Don Lee). Following reports in March that NetEase, the studio's source of funding, would be pulling said funding in May due to ballooning costs reaching around seven billion yen, the time has sadly come for Nagoshi Studio, having not found any alternative funding sources in the time since.

Gang of Dragon looked very much to be 'just Like a Dragon again', which I find to be something of a depressing fate for a studio headed by the original series' creator. Having left Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio following Judgment and Yakuza: Like a Dragon, two of its most innovative games both with new protagonists and one entirely new turn-based gameplay style, it feels indicative of the industry that Nagoshi was granted funding seemingly on the condition that the studio makes something that just looks like the rest of the Like a Dragon series. I love Ma Dong-seok as an actor, but his presence was one of the more blatant, 'look, we got that guy!' castings of the LAD archetype, which is saying something considering Infinite Wealth had fucking Danny Trejo in a prominent role. The trailer closing with a shot of Dong-seok framed by Kabukicho's torii gate, maybe the most famous image from the Like a Dragon series, put a sour taste in my mouth as being just more of the same brand recognition (yet, for a new IP!) to prioritise safe return on investment.

I'm unfortunately not that surprised to see Gang of Dragon and Nagoshi Studio lost to time, though I am sad about it. I have some conflicted feelings on Nagoshi as a person/auteur, but I don't think he, or his studio, deserves to have funding pulled before they could even release anything as a result of NetEase deciding to pull investments out of non-Chinese companies over time. It's unknown what Nagoshi and the team will be attempting next, but I truly hope they can eventually make something. No More Heroes studio Grasshopper Manufacture was able to detach themselves from NetEase very recently and possibly avoid a similar fate, so it might not be impossible.

"We will do our utmost in developing Stellar Blade: Blood Rain to live up to this interest"

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Shift Up says Stellar Blade: Blood Rain is making solid progress toward reaching the quality highs the developers expect, and that more will be revealed "in stages." And if that doesn't get you excited, The Weeknd has played it and is a big fan.

As part of a new financial briefing to investors, the top brass at Shift Up has been taking questions about what's currently going on behind the scenes. One of which is, simply, how is Stellar Blade: Blood Rain getting on?

"Development of Stellar Blade: Blood Rain is progressing toward our target quality level under the principle of securing sufficient development time to deliver the highest level of completeness," Shift Up says, "and we plan to disclose information about the game in stages."

That means it's going alright, if you were wondering. Shift Up has previously spoken about setting a high bar and ensuring what the devs are making clears it with flying colors before putting a game in the public's hands. It's all pretty common speak when it comes to investor reports, though what comes next is anything but.

"Recently, global pop star The Weeknd visited our headquarters during his trip to Korea, toured the development floor, played the build in development first-hand and shared his affection for Stellar Blade," Shift Up continues. "This shows that Stellar Blade is establishing itself as a global IP drawing attention beyond gaming into the wider cultural sphere, and we will do our utmost in developing Stellar Blade: Blood Rain to live up to this interest."

I ain't here to tell people what they should like or not like, but it's the first time – and maybe last? – I've seen The Weeknd mentioned in an investor report. You know, those reports that are filled with numbers and are put together for people who are mainly interested in labor costs and ask why you can't just release more games to make more money while spending less money.

Anyway, I wonder if our Star Boy has played Goddess of Victory: Nikke. Much to ponder.

#4052. "It's Terrific" - Take-Two Boss Acknowledges Zelda Remake's High Score Ahead Of GTA VI Launch

There's been a lot of conversation online about the Zelda remake and Grand Theft Auto going head-to-head this month.

GamesBeat has now asked the Take-Two Interactive boss Strauss Zelnick what he thinks about this and Ocarina of Time's current Metacritic score of 96/100.

He politely responded, stating the game's score is "terrific" and Nintendo should be "very proud of the title".

As for the idea of the two games competing against each other, the CEO of Rockstar's parent company didn't really acknowledge any direct "competition", but more broadly, believes "you compete against everything and nothing" in the entertainment business.

"In the entertainment business, you compete against everything and nothing. Everything because there’s so many ways consumers can spend their time, and nothing because if there’s nothing good out there, people don’t need to consume any of it. It’s like food; like food could be bad, but you still are going to be hungry. But in the case of entertainment, it’s not a must-have; it’s a want to have. So it’s our job to make the best entertainment on earth. When we do that, people will show up for it.”

In his words, if it's the "best entertainment on earth", then "people will show up for it".

While Zelda's Ocarina remake has done tremendously well for Nintendo, and early reports suggest its sales are off to a positive start in certain locations, Grand Theft Auto VI (at least for now) has been labelled the most anticipated launch of all time. Presales of the new entry have already exceeded expectations, and it's a digital-only release, with retail copies sold as a "code-in-a-box" release.

And if you're wondering about the possibility of a Switch 2 version, Nintendo of America's president has recently said it's a "conversation for Take-Two and Rockstar". Earlier this week, Rockstar also confirmed GTA VI will run at 30fps on PlayStation 5, PS5 Pro and Xbox Series X|S. It will be available on Xbox One through Xbox Cloud Gaming, too.

#4051. Microsoft Announces Last-Minute Restock Of The Xbox Series X25 Console

Available at launch through the Microsoft Store and participating retailers

Ever since the Xbox Series X25 console first became available for pre-order in August, it's become hard to get your hands on one. The "Limited Edition" system quickly sold out, and became a target for scalpers within 24 hours as well.

If you were hoping to add the Series X25 to your collection (or the accompanying controller, for that matter), you might still have a chance - Microsoft says that a "limited" restock will be available on November 12th to mark the launch.

This apparently goes live at "midnight local time", which we assume means November 11th going into November 12th (although the tweet doesn't make this fully clear):

As you can see, the restock will be available on the official Microsoft Store / Xbox Store, but also at other participating retailers that have yet to be named. We assume most of them will be the ones that carried the original pre-order.

You can feel free to go back to our pre-order guide for the Xbox Series X25 console if you want easy to access to various links and pricing info, but just be aware that things might be a bit different for this restock, so it's worth searching around at midnight local time if the Microsoft Store version sells out quickly.

Are you hoping to get your hands on one of these? Let us know down in the comments section below!

#4050. The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel teaser all but confirms Hammerfell setting and means we can finally stop using that eight year old header image with the hills

Say hello to sandy scroll screengrab for the foreseeable future

Praise Talos and whatever other Elder Scrolls deities you might worship. We here at RPS and in the wider gaming press finally have new material to use when hunting for images to symbolise The Elder Scrolls 6. No more will we be limited to that shot of some hills from the 2018 teaser, because Bethesda have shown off an elder scroll covered in sand while revealing the new game's subtitle and all but locking in a setting. As a recent report from The Verge claimed, it's called The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel and looks to be set in Hammerfell.

These details were revealed in a short teaser at the end of a Todd Howard-fronted video celebrating Bethesda Game Studios' 40th anniversary. As such, the majority of the video is the Toddinator recapping the studio's history by touching on each of the games they've put out since 1986's Gridiron. Then, he looks to the future. "You know, everybody’s always asking about Elder Scrolls 6," the Toddfather said. "And we thought, hey, given the moment, what a perfect time to tell you what The Elder Scrolls 6 is actually called."

Cue a shot of an elder scroll buried in sand, followed by the The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel in fancy logo font. Then, a quote attributed to a moth priest called Yazar. "The scroll offered only a shimmer, a veil thinly lifted to my eyes. A future lost. A victory undone. Sands of time scattered by fate." OOH, CRYPTIC. In all seriousness, between the subtitle, the sand, and Yazar being referred to as a moth priest in service of High Queen Iradne of Hammerfell, the Verge report's assertion that the game will be set in Hammerfell is essentially set in stone by this teaser even if his Toddliness didn't spell it out himself.

Sentinel's the name of both a kingdom and city in the Redguards' province. The inclusion of an elder scroll in the teaser and the quote from Yazar also lend credence to the Verge report's claim that the game will make a big thing out of unravelling secrets linked to the provenance of these mysterious bits of paper. As for the quote's yammering of lost futures and undone victories, I'll venture to speculate that it could turn out to be reference to the player character thwarting a Thalmor victory, since Skyrim seemed to set up the elves as being on the verge of conquering Tamriel as the Cyrodillic empire fractured and fell.

That may or may not be the case, but we do know for sure that this teaser likely means a huge downturn in use of the header image below. It's eight years old, pulled from The Elder Scrolls 6's infamous 2018 teaser. All these years on, the game's finally on the way. You've served us well, screengrab of some hills. Talos guide you to wherever less regularly used images go.

Elder Scrolls teasing aside, it's worth bearing in mind that Bethesda parent company Microsoft have spent the majority of this year gutting their workforce with mass layoffs and studio ditching. Microsoft are also still currently subject to a BDS movement boycott over their reported ties to the Israeli military.

#4049. Poll: Is GTA 6 Being Stuck at 30fps on PS5 a Dealbreaker?

Your (potential) nightmare has become a reality: GTA 6 runs at just 30 frames-per-second on PS5 and PS5 Pro.

The target frame rate was confirmed earlier today by Rockstar Games itself, prompting an outpouring of relative disappointment from those who were banking on a silky 60fps experience.

Of course, 30fps isn't the end of the world — as long as it's nice and stable — but there's no getting away from the fact that the vast majority of games on PS5 offer some form of higher frame rate.

Most AAA releases, for example, provide a choice between a 30fps 'quality' mode, which trades frames for increased visual clarity, and a 60fps 'performance' mode, which usually sacrifices resolution for smoother gameplay.

News GTA 6 PS5 Pro Features Revealed, 30fps Target on Both Consoles

Improved clarity and ray traced shadows on PS5 Pro

GTA 6 will offer no such compromise, presumably because it's so beefed up in the graphical department.

Indeed, early tech analyses have pointed out that this could be one of the most graphically intensive games ever made; an open world effort that goes beyond anything the genre's seen up until now.

The bottom line here is that you'd like to think Rockstar knows what it's doing. If it had to keep the frame rate capped at 30 to deliver on its vision of a modern Vice City, then that's the long and short of it.

Although having said that, I'm sure there are plenty of people out there who would have happily taken a graphical hit to have GTA 6 run at 60fps. I might be one of them!

But is GTA 6's lack of 60fps a dealbreaker for you? Might you actually avoid playing it now that only 30fps is confirmed? Vote in our polls, and then move at a higher frame rate in the comments section below.

Guide GTA 6 Release Times and Preload: When Can You Start Playing?

Robert (or Rob if you're lazy) is an assistant editor of Push Square, and has been a fan of PlayStation since the 90s, when Tekken 2 introduced him to the incredible world of video games. He still takes his fighting games seriously, but RPGs are his true passion. The Witcher, Persona, Dragon Quest, Mass Effect, Final Fantasy, Trails, Tales — he's played 'em all. A little too much, some might say.

It's not a graphics issue. It's a simulation issue. The game has been designed around the PS5's CPU, and there's no graphical compromise that would make 60 fps possible. Or even 40, for that matter.

GTA VI apparently has no performance headroom. It's probably optimized to the bones. That's why it looks like nothing we've seen before (both visuals and gameplay).

The Pro CPU is clocked 10% faster than base. If there's no headroom, you simply won't sustain 40 fps. Remember:

@Art_Vandelay I know next to nothing about what goes on “under the hood” regardless of whether I’m playing on PS5, PC or XBox. So please forgive the noob question.

@NavalHistorian It's kind of both: the CPU handles everything that happens on and off screen, but from a logic standpoint. Imagine you close your eyes and an agent from the game's Matrix starts narrating everything that's happening at any given moment. This is the CPU. Now, imagine that there's another agent that listens to that description and simply paints the frames without really thinking about the logic. That's the GPU.

If the CPU agent can't describe the action quickly enough for the GPU agent to render it, then it doesn't matter how fast the GPU is. You're CPU-bound.

And to answer your second question, the reason Sony opted for a rather small performance bump on the Pro's CPU side is probably a mix of compatibility/stability/reliability and cost. I mean, they could have moved to a better manufacturing process node and got a bigger frequency bump, but that would have made the console much more expensive. Or they could have moved to a newer architecture, which would dramatically increase R&D costs and ultimately raise the price as well, while posing compatibility risks with existing games.

You see, the GPU is way easier to scale, which explains why Sony (and Microsoft) opted for proportionally beefier GPU bumps for the PS4 Pro, the Xbox One X and the PS5 Pro.

#4048. Mobile Suit Gundam Battle Operation 3 has been announced, marking another attempt at a free-to-play team game after Gundam Evolution's unfortunate fate

Bandai Namco have released the initial announcement trailer for Mobile Suit Gundam Battle Operation 3, a free-to-play team action game and a sequel to 2018's Battle Operation 2. The trailer is very, very pretty, showing off Gundam units clashing in large-scale battles and infantry fighting beneath the colossal mechas' feet (kinda like Titanfall, in having both human and mecha players in the same match). I'm sadly not yet enough of a true Gundam fan to recognise many of these units on sight other than the RX-78-2, but there's a real variety shown off here.

MOBILE SUIT GUNDAM GUNDAM BATTLE OPERATION 3　Announcement Trailer Watch on YouTube

While there's no release date specified in the trailer, Bandai Namco have confirmed that there will be a network test in Japan through November 20th-22nd, with an open network test planned for the future (thanks, Gematsu).

Following the fate of Gundam Evolution, a 2022 attempt at a hero shooter featuring Gundam units, it's nice to see another shot at taking the Gundam series into a team format. Evolution suffered from the all-too-common trappings of heavy microtransaction inclusion, with several playable Gundam units with unique abilities only available through paying real cash. It was rightly criticised for this, and since Bandai Namco seemed to have had high hopes for the revenue it could make from said microtransactions, the lack of money made meant it shut down just a year later.

Contrastingly, from what I can see, Gundam Battle Operation 2 was received fairly well on its release. While little is actually known about the third game at this point, let's hope it has a better chance than the series' last big release. I will quickly note that the trailer does close with a "*Some content may require purchase" note, so it'll likely have some form of microtransaction in itself — hopefully not to the same degree as Evolution. And, while we're on the topic of Gundam, there's also 2027's Gundam Rogue Orbit, a drastically different game that seems closer to a Devil May Cry-esque action title (though, unlike Battle Operation 3, will begin life as a timed exclusive to PS5). Now, if we could get a Gundam game that plays something like Armored Core, and god willing a proper PC release, I would be a very happy girl.

#4047. GTA 6 Gets Its First Unboxing Video As Shipping Begins For Xbox & PS5

Here's a look at what's inside the physical edition

While Rockstar Games mentioned a date of November 12th for shipping the physical edition of GTA 6 for Xbox and PS5 the other day, we noticed other retailers stating the 11th instead, so it's no surprise that it's showing up in the wild.

The first unboxing video for GTA 6 seemingly arrived overnight, racking up over 1 million views already on social media since it was posted. This specific video is for the PS5 version, but we expect no major differences for the Xbox version.

Since this was posted, other unboxing videos have also started to hit the web, like you see in the YouTube video at the top of this article. It clearly shows that GTA 6 comes with a download code, a separate code for Ultimate Edition content where applicable, and a double-sided poster as had been confirmed previously.

It also now affirms that the poster contains the GTA 6 cover art on the front, and a piece of artwork for a female character on the back - not Lucia or Jason, but presumably a character that's heavily involved in the story regardless.

We've obviously talked a bit about the physical edition of GTA 6 already this week, and you can vote in the poll below if you didn't get a chance the first time, but we thought an actual unboxing video was worth a bit of extra coverage - an opportunity to see exactly what you'll be getting inside the physical edition if you've opted for it.

#4046. Venom-toothed Noxious Terminids are soon to infest Helldivers 2, and it's your noble job to sterilise the galaxy for Super Earth

Helldivers 2 isn't slowing down any time soon, and according to Edwin's recent interview with Arrowhead CCO Johan Pilestedt, it'll continue to be Arrowhead's main priority for the future. As if Helldivers 2 wasn't full of enough horrors for our brave Super Earth Helldivers to shoot at for the betterment of galactic democracy, its next update is due to add an entirely new Terminid subspecies, the Noxious Terminids.

First up on are the Noxious Scavengers. These horrible little (see: huge) things skitter around at high speed and are loaded with deadly poison, but are thankfully at least fragile. Liberal use of area-of-effect weapons such as flamethrowers, explosives and flamethrowers are recommended to avoid being overrun by these horse-sized insects. Then there's the Noxious Spewer, which is not only fast like its smaller brethren despite its larger size, but also equipped with a web projectile which locks a Helldiver in place, vulnerable to a fatal bite. Oh, and if you dare shoot its soft underbelly, it violently explodes, with the same web fluid covering a wide area around it. The poison inflicted by these creatures' bites is a new damage over time effect that can blur vision, slow movement, eat away at your health, and make you fear this may be the end for you — so it's a bit like getting the flu (get your jabs!)

HELLDIVERS™ 2 | A Cleaner Galaxy Starts With You Watch on YouTube

This update also makes the change that bug caves can be found across many more worlds across the galaxy, leading troopers down tunnels with limited visibility and claustrophobic dead ends. Super Earth's propaganda, sorry, I mean, guidance, describes the galactic sterilisation program quite simply: locate the invasive species, identify the horrific monsters at the barrel of your flamethrower, and sterilise (burn to cinders). The guidance also, hilariously, includes the line: "Super Earth reminds you that ammunition is cheaper than antivenom." Now, get out there and rid our beautiful democracy of this vile pestilence.

#4045. World of Warcraft: Forever review: "A love letter to the MMORPG I fell for over 20 years ago"

Keep exploring and earning more as a member.

Get the biggest gaming news, reviews, and releases straight to your inbox.

Join the GamesRadar community for quick access. Enter your email below and we'll send confirmation, and sign you up to our newsletter.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

World of Warcraft: Forever is a love letter to why we all fell for it in 2005. It still has a familiar charm but it adds on extra areas, extra quests, and a plethora of fantastic user interface improvements which makes it feel far more modern than before. It's everything that veteran players have longed for.

A beautiful reinvention of a much-loved MMO

User interface changes and tweaks are improvements

It's still World of Warcraft at heart, so it won't convert naysayers

Why you can trust GamesRadar+ Our experts review games, movies and tech over countless hours, so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about our reviews policy.

As I created a Hunter in World of Warcraft: Forever for what must be the 100th time by now, the saying 'the definition of insanity is doing the same thing over and over again and expecting different results' rolled around my head a lot. I've played this game before. A lot. Is Forever truly sufficiently different to be so obsessed again? Well, yes. It's this lovely, warm, flawed, wonderfully infuriating dose of nostalgia. It's simultaneously far improved from the original World of Warcraft and, more recently, World of Warcraft Classic (we'll get into the differences shortly), while leaving you with questions of 'why would you leave that in?'.

Will it convert those who never liked WoW in the first place? Of course not. I don't think that's the point of World of Warcraft: Forever. Instead, it brings home all those slightly lost souls from 20+ years ago (AKA millennials like me who want to return to familiar comfort once more), but with some core improvements. It does that incredibly well and given it has brought back a record number of lapsed players, so far it's succeeding.

I've been playing World of Warcraft since the closed beta days in 2004. I've reviewed many World of Warcraft expansion packs (including my WoW: Midnight review this year), played Classic substantially, and have now skipped meals and sleep in favor of playing Forever. I've played seemingly every other mainstream MMO you can think of too, and should probably learn to step away from the PC more often but the allure of WoW remains too strong. – Reviewer Jen Allen

Release date: November 4, 2026Platform(s): PCDeveloper: In-housePublisher: Blizzard Entertainment

Before I dive too deep, let's sum up the differences between World of Warcraft, World of Warcraft Classic, and World of Warcraft Forever so you actually know why the game's important. Retail is best seen as an entirely different beast to Forever. It's very fast-paced, throws nearly as many unlocks at you as a standard game of Fortnite, and is all about leveling up as fast as possible to get to the next part of the story. Getting from level 1 to the level cap of 80 can take just 10 hours if you know what you're doing. It has its place for sure and I really like it, but it's far removed from World of Warcraft's launch years, which is where Classic comes in.

Classic took the game right back to the start and has gradually introduced expansion packs in chronological order. It has a linear progression path, while its leveling process is slow-paced. Each level is richly earned and you'll spend around 200 hours or more playing to reach the level cap of 70. Crucially, not much has been done to spruce anything up. There are some odd UI choices, it looks increasingly dated, and it feels old. It's familiar and fun but also fairly rough around the edges once you start looking.

World of Warcraft: Forever takes what many loved about Classic, but with some key quality-of-life improvements. Player level is permanently capped at 60 with horizontal rather than vertical progression. Oh, and there's a new race called the Skyborne and a bunch of new race/class combinations. You'd be forgiven for thinking Forever still sounds a lot like Classic from this brief overview. It kind of is. But, it's better. This feels like a take on World of Warcraft Classic fans like me wanted, truer to the original experience but willing to remix its approach to deliver new sensations as well.

I spent dozens of hours playing the World of Warcraft: Forever beta, and I've already put dozens more into the full release. I'm not alone either. Friends are excited about it again and the servers are packed. I've yet to see them prohibitively packed though. Forever uses a new layering system whereby players pick how they want to play the game (Normal, PvP, or Roleplay) and that's it. There are no pesky issues with 'oh no, my friend chose a different server to me and now we can't play' with the game shrewdly keeping an eye on its layers and moving people around as and when that layer gets full to the point it would degrade the play experience.

It mostly works. Early on, friends and I found that we had to manually reset the layer by logging out and back into the game, but after the first day, it worked seamlessly. Such a move is an early example of how Forever is designed to be far more accessible for all.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

Right from the start, you're actually guided through the game with a helpful early tutorial teaching you how to move, attack, and what to do when you die for the first time. As a veteran player, I didn't need it, but I could see the substantial benefit. Retail has a tutorial, but Classic never bothered with one. Another point in favor of this iteration.

Diving in is a beautiful experience once more, especially if you roll one of the new Skyborne race characters. Affectionately referred to as blue Smurfs, these elves are wondrous. They look great amongst a game with improved looking models but none that can rival this new race. You can play either as Alliance or Horde with the Skyborne, with Druid, Hunter, Rogue, and Warrior available for all, while Horde and Alliance have Mage and Shaman classes at their disposal respectively.

There are specific Skyborne racial abilities which are useful too. Walk on Air allows you to glide in the air for 10 seconds which I found a great timesaver when wanting to fall from high distances. There's also Skysight for Horde which boosts run speed by 10%, while Alliance can activate a ley line and gain 100% increased health and mana regeneration for a time. Throughout my time playing WoW, I tend to forget to use my racial abilities – but these are the kind of skills I didn't want to miss out on.

Skyborne also has some delightful new animations such as a unique dance, a cute cheer, and a more appealing jump than most. Druids get new forms as well. It all feels very fresh once more. After extensively leveling with Skyborne, I didn't want to go back to the legacy races. The Skyborne starter zone of Zephras Isle is luscious. It has that typical World of Warcraft feel to it but it's sprawling, colorful, and a gorgeous reflection of how far games have come.

The water effects across the game are more realistic with waves moving naturally, and the lighting reflecting how it should be compared to real life. Even the audio is slightly muffled when you're underwater, although I found I needed good headphones to absorb this fully. There are some great looking weather effects too. Seeing The Barrens on a hot summer's day then the next day encountering bad storms and fog is special.

None of this would matter much if Forever wasn't fun but it is so much fun. Right now, everyone in-game is as welcoming as they were during the original days. I easily found pickup groups but also I'd have random players resurrect me just because they could, or toss me a heal at a key moment. Another time, I was boarding a zeppelin outside of Orgrimmar and the ship was full of shamans in wolf form dancing and encouraging everyone else to join in.

The ship was full of shamans in wolf form dancing and encouraging everyone else to join in.

After years of World of Warcraft feeling lonely and more of a solo MMO, Forever has united players again. At points, I'd be in a silent group, but at others, we'd chat and share our experiences. My Hunter teamed up with a Druid for one quest, and even though neither of us spoke the same language so we communicated through emotes. It was a beautiful moment when we succeeded.

There are new dungeons too covering all level ranges. Hall of Thanes is an early addition for levels 13-18 and it isn't just a matter of 'run and smash' with a bit more strategy easing you into the dungeon mentality, before hitting Ruins of Lordaeron at 15-20, Excavation Site: Wetlands in the 20s, and more beyond that. There's a rich variety here with experience bonuses varying a little while Blizzard balances things. I don't live in dungeons but I've enjoyed diving in to break up the exploration side of the game.

Forever also encourages community spirit with its campfire system. Feeling delightfully RPGish, you can plonk down a campfire and share some buffs with other players. It ties into cooking well, but ultimately it gives you a moment to reflect. While exploring, I've come across plenty of players just camping and chilling. It's a nice reminder that you're playing an MMO, an active world full of players making their own way.

There are still predictable moments of tedium, of course. While Forever has much faster respawns than other versions of the game (sometimes too fast to keep up with in quieter areas), quest item drops can be very hit and miss. At one point, I spent a disproportionate amount of time trying to collect satyr horns from mobs. I needed 16. They only seemed to drop about every 10 mobs despite me being able to see the horns on the satyrs. A boring reminder that sometimes, you'll still be simply grinding away in-game rather than absorbing those beautiful moments of unity.

After 22 years, World of Warcraft: Forever has finally sold me on Blizzard's undying MMO – now I never want to leave

Combat is mostly much how it's always been. There's autoattack via one key press (or button on the action bar) and then you choose other actions such as casting a particular spell, buff, or special attack.

There's now gamepad support which has opened the game up to unofficial Steam Deck support via a few tweaks. I found this worked well enough. Much like Final Fantasy 14's implementation of gamepad support on console, I wouldn't fancy my chances using a gamepad during more intense moments such as dungeons or raids. It's just not quite as precise or as speedy as a traditional mouse and keyboard setup. It is handy for casual play though, and for those times you don't want to be hunched over your keyboard. Ultimately, more choice is only ever a good thing.

Curiously, while Forever has made the game smaller by not implementing expansion packs, it also feels much bigger as exploration is mostly conducted on foot until you can afford a ground mount (no flying mounts here) but it means everything you achieve feels richly earned.

For the most part, Forever is a wondrous success. The game I'm itching to play more of even though it's all I've done for days. There are so many good tweaks that make it better than Classic. A recent ally alert pops up next to players you've recently grouped with, there's Discord integration which was previously only on Retail, and the quest limit is now up to 40 from 20 (incredibly convenient if you're like me and stockpile quest hand-ins).

The promised 1,000 or so new quests are interspersed nicely with many of the early ones linking together zones more cohesively, and introducing professions and other valuable skills well. Some simply provide you with good gear like bags or a weapon that helps you feel strong for a few levels. All the new quests I've experienced feel like they deserved to be there rather than feeling like filler to pad out the experience.

I'm curious about what will happen further down the line for the game. There's a roadmap lined up for new raids in December before we get even more new raids, dungeons, and quests in 2027, so the next 12 months should be pretty exciting. From there, who knows? WoW: Forever focuses on horizontal progression so we won't see a level cap increase but that makes sense for a game that's all about the journey rather than the destination.

As in life, it's a smart move to enjoy the ride rather than think too far ahead and I haven't had this much fun with World of Warcraft in decades. Sometimes that's all you need. Now, if you'll excuse me, I have a Skyborne Hunter seeking my attention. I want to make some new gear for my guild and get raid ready. The good times are finally back.

World of Warcraft: Forever was reviewed on PC, with a code provided by the publisher.

Planning to play forever? Check out our best open world games and best RPGs rankings for more to play now, and keep an eye on our upcoming RPGs calendar for what's on the horizon!

#4043. Frostpunk 2's The Surge DLC keeps the wintery apocalypse and adds in faction-clash-inducing electricity and sets a seasonally appropriate December release date

For the time being, the world of Frostpunk remains a hypothetical, even if it's one that seems just that little bit more likely than I'd like it to be given who's in charge of the world. But at the very least, there are pockets of hope to be found in Frostpunk 2, namely with its newly revealed next bit of DLC, The Surge, a name that has been bequeathed to it for incredibly obvious reasons. Oh, you need me to explain them? Fiiiiine.

You and your probably not so merry band of survivors have been trekking across the UK, when you end up at a "mysterious valley." Apparently some rumours have been going round about a "marvel left behind by history’s greatest mind - a relic with the potential to reshape the world itself." So you go off to look for it, and it essentially seems like this relic lets you use a whole bunch of electricity. Only, despite how useful this is for automating a bunch of work, various factions disagree over how it should be used, "while the secrets hidden within the valley prove far more difficult to uncover than anyone expected."

In terms of what you should expect from this DLC, for starters there's a new scenario to check out "set in an entirely new region, far beyond the borders explored in Frostpunk 2 so far." This relic is also implied to have come from the mind of one Nikola Tesla, you know, the electricity guy. There'll apparently be ways to utilise the Great Storm that's ruined the planet to "turn catastrophic whiteouts into valuable, harvested and stored resources." And you'll have some hidden treasures to find and mysterious to uncover in various nearby caves and ruins.

All sounds neat enough! And it's not too far away either. The Surge is currently slated for a seasonally appropriate December 14th release date. Let's hope no real world environmental disasters get in the way of that, 'ey? While you wait for it, you can wishlist the DLC on Steam.

#4042. The Outer Worlds 2 PS5 DLC Split into Two Parts, First in December

Obsidian still wants to carry out its post-launch DLC plans for The Outer Worlds 2, having lost 25% of its workforce in a recent round of layoffs. It's today announced an expansion called Side Effect Guaranteed will release in two parts: the first launches for PS5 on 2nd December 2026, and then the second arrives in Spring 2027. See it in action in the trailer.

The new DLC takes place just before the end of the main game, so if you've already finished a playthrough, there'll be a new option on the starting menu screen that lets you access the content through a new character.

A distress signal beckons you and your crew of the Incognito to a derelict ship, where you discover the ship’s crew in suspended animation. All signs point to foul play, especially the puddle of what was most likely a person that you recover a video message from. It was left by the captain of the vessel, who explains that the crew has been contaminated with something while on a heist that will cause explosive cell death unless they find a cure. And by explosive cell death, she means more like a… “liquefaction”.

Side Effect Guaranteed adds a new region to explore called Elysium Valley, another recruitable character, a level cap increase to 36, more than 15 new perks, four extra flaws, and additional gear (weapons, armour, and outfits). You can also look forward to an additional 20 songs.

The expansion costs $14.99, or if you bought the Premium Edition of the game, you'll gain instant access to the DLC.

Review The Outer Worlds 2 (PS5) - Mechanically Fantastic RPG Struggles to Be Memorable

It'll work to expand and improve an RPG we thought was pretty good at release, awarding it a 7/10 rating. "The Outer Worlds 2 succeeds in being a bigger and better sequel, buoyed by an even greater emphasis on player choice and freedom. Its RPG mechanics are largely fantastic, and there are key improvements to both combat and exploration," we said at the time. "However, despite Obsidian's clever writing, there's an underlying dreariness to the property that it just can't seem to escape."

#4041. Xbox Brings Halo's Iconic Pelican To Microsoft Flight Sim 2024 As Limited-Time Freebie

Act fast and claim the combat dropship for free!

Asobo Studios is commemorating the 25th anniversary of Halo by introducing the iconic UNSC Pelican into Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024.

Over the years, the combat dropshop has seen a plethora of talented pilots don its cockpit: Carol 'Foehammer' Rawley, the reluctant Fernando Esparza, and now you!

"Designed and built by Misriah Armory, the D77 Pelican has a typical crew of three (pilot, copilot, and crew chief) and can carry up to 14 fully outfitted infantry and their equipment. A vehicle can be carried in the external hardpoint clamp for immediate deployment. It has a lifting body design powered by four high-efficiency fusion thrusters with secondary positional / stability augmenters. The wings have three hardpoints each, which can hold sensors, cargo pods, or weapons."

Halo turns 25 alongside Xbox this Sunday, on November 15. So, we've seen iteration after iteration of the sci-fi shooter's most recognisable ship, which has traditionally only been pilotable in the previous MSFS and Halo 4's 'Shutdown' mission. There are other, more difficult means, to cheese your way into flying the Pelican across other Halo games, but now you don't have to.

The D77-TC Pelican in Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 offers:

Personally, even though MSFS isn't my cup of tea, getting to roleplay what it'd been like to ferry Master Chief across the ring is something I'm definitely interested in trying. I really do enjoy when Halo vehicles show up in other games. From time to time, I stick on Halo 2's scorpion mix, hop into Forza Horizon 5 and take the Warthog for a spin. Just for the vibes.

If you're keen to fly the Halo Pelican in Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024, you'd best act quick, because it's only free between November 10-17, and then $9.99 afterwards.

Here's where you need to go to complete Heart of the Fist in Phantom Blade Zero

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The Phantom Blade Zero Heart of the Fist side quest is a very simple one, tasking you with finding the grave of the Iron Fist Master and leaving some incense there for the Iron Fiend. Unfortunately, the only hint that the game gives you is that the grave is in the Mirrorwood. Thankfully, it's not very far at all and you will have walked past the grave at least once or twice while playing through Phantom Blade, so this is where to find it.

The Iron Fist Master's grave is very close to the Burial Grounds Bell on the eastern side of the Crimson Forest. Fast travel to this location, then head over to the large grave in the middle of this icy clearing.

Interact with this grave and you'll see a cutscene of Soul burning some incense to honor the fallen master. You'll then immediately be rewarded with the Fist Fragment: Shell item which automatically combines with the Fist Fragment: Core you got after fighting the Iron Fiend the first time. They form the Worldbreaker Fist, which is the necessary item for Soul Tempering the Iron Gauntlets Phantom Edge.And that's the end of Heart of the Fist! Now you should carry on exploring the frozen parts of the Crimson Forest. I recommend going back to the Sha-Chi Tower and sparring with the Jade Dancer and Iron Fiend for the 'Use It Against Them' quest if you haven’t already, as this is how you get the Soul Tempering item for the Fiend Saws dual swords. Then you can finish off the Phantom Blade Zero Triple Threat quest by getting to the end of the forest and facing the Phantom Blade Zero Three-Faced Puppet once again.
